title: Portfolio Standing across a Host's Keyturn Host Protection Plan Enrolments
content:
A host's enrolments are read as one portfolio when the marketplace judges standing, even though cover under the Keyturn Host Protection Plan is written vehicle by vehicle.

1. Accepted claims are counted across every enrolment the host holds over the rolling twelve months, and it is that portfolio count, not the count on the vehicle being claimed on, that decides whether the host goes in front of a reviewer or has cover suspended.
2. The rolling twelve months are counted back from the day the matter is handled, that day included, and the count is of appraisals accepted across every enrolment the host holds.
3. An unpaid host liability on any one enrolment blocks a new enrolment for the same host, because the marketplace does not extend fresh cover to a host who owes it money on cover already given.
4. Where a host holds enrolments on several plans the strictest standing rule among the plans held applies to the portfolio, and the most generous plan never softens the review threshold of the others.

### The authority for clause 3

Whether a host liability stands unpaid is read, before the new enrolment is written, from the amount owed by the host standing on the host's own enrolment records, matched to the host by the member the enrolments are held under. A host's account of what they have paid is not what settles it.

### Points of judgement

| Situation | Standing |
|---|---|
| Two accepted claims on one vehicle, one on another, all within the rolling twelve months | Three accepted claims count to the portfolio. |
| A host holds one enrolment on a plan whose published review threshold is 2 and another whose threshold is 5 | The stricter threshold of 2 governs the portfolio. |
| A host owes an unpaid liability on a lapsed enrolment and applies for a new vehicle | The new enrolment is blocked while that liability stands unpaid. |
